analysis: Documentation-only PR touching docs/reference/configuration.md (head excerpt, lines 503-576) and docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md (patch hunks at lines 228 and 280). Its security-relevant content is a documented behavior change in the SSD prefix-cache tier (T-041, A-001, TB-007): on Macs with >=96 GiB RAM, complete-checkpoint staging caps rise from 1024 MiB/1000 ms to 3072 MiB/2500 ms. DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_MAX_STAGE_MB and _MS now also override these large-memory defaults. The docs state the daily write cap is unchanged. The doc says it admits about 16,384 restored Qwen 3.8 tokens instead of 8,192. This affects read/staging admission, not at-rest exposure: DBK3 crypto, HMAC naming, the 1800 s TTL, the disk budget and the write budget are unchanged, so T-041 mitigations (a)-(e) are not weakened. The staging limit bounds transient host/native RAM through GlobalKVCacheBudget. The doc says native destination plus bounded scratch is reserved before allocation, with no permanent RAM carve. That is consistent with the T-041 no-carve posture. Larger staging could slightly widen the local availability and memory-pressure surface (relevant to T-010 and T-029 style DoS concerns). It is gated by reservation and by the >=96 GiB threshold, and I found no evidence of a regression. A larger cache-hit window could marginally extend the same-account TTFT oracle (SEC-035). That is accepted in kind, and T-041's description does not need updating for this. The source code (SSDPrefixCachePolicy.swift, SSDHybridCheckpointStoreFactory.swift) was not supplied, so the doc claims about reservation and caps are unverified. The next pass should confirm that the implementation actually reserves before allocation and honors the explicit env overrides. The env vars are not on the LaunchAgent allow-list, so only foreground use applies. The rest of the changes are the date bump and a table row edit.
